newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shot in shoulder near premier's house.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shot in shoulder near premier's house.

text.p: Egyptian police shot a man in the shoulder on Saturday afternoon in an incident about 200 metres (yards) from the Cairo home of Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, interior ministry officials said.
The London-based television station Middle East Broadcasting Company (MBC) described the incident as an attempt to assassinate Ganzouri but the ministry denied this.
"An official security source affirms that this report has no basis in truth," a ministry statement said.
It said a policeman suspected and approached a man in the street in the suburb of Heliopolis, where Ganzouri lives.
The statement said the man took him to a car to show him his papers, took a revolver out of the glovebox and fired two shots in the air.
The car, which had two other men inside, drove off and the policeman fired one bullet through the back window.
Police stopped the car some miles away and arrested the three men. One of them, named as Mahmoud Ashmawi, had a bullet wound in the left shoulder, the ministry added.
The ministry said two of the three men had criminal records for theft from cars and the other was on parole and alleged that the men had gone to the area with plans to rob people.
